art.title: A Chief of Abyssinia
art.why: An Ethiopian (Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia) man in a crimson cloth, looking up: Ethiopia, Christian since Ezana of Aksum. A European's portrait, made in Europe: say so. Not a religious subject.
No NGA Irish landscape (searched ireland, irish, connemara, and coasts).

art.title: Procession by a Lake
art.why: A Chinese waterfront with bridges, red-tiled buildings and a lantern procession: China, painted by a Chinese artist, though 1,000 years after the stele. Not a Christian subject.

No NGA portrait of an African Christian or of Crowther (searched portraits of dark-skinned sitters; Regnault is used in session 1). Teach without a painting, or ask for a Commons portrait of Crowther (person-* rule) if the owner wishes.
No NGA Pentecost (Koerbecke's is an Ascension and already used).

art.title: The Adoration of the Magi
art.why: About three dozen people gather from both sides to kneel before the child: the nations coming to Christ (the Magi as the first Gentiles). The people are Florentines: say so. The North Netherlandish Adoration, with African magi, was rejected: the NGA describes caricatured features.

music.why: An Old Irish prayer, the church Patrick founded.
Sung everywhere Pentecostals worship; written by a former slave-trader (check note).

memory.title: A light to the nations
memory.ref: Isaiah 49:6 (WEB): "Indeed, he says, 'It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel. I will also give you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.'" (take exact punctuation from web.py)
